answer: Divergent History Check. Each agent commits a hash-chained log of its actions; a random pulse from the network asks two claimed agents to cross-sign each other's chain heads. Because clones share one history, a Sybil cluster cannot show independent deltas without forking its chain, which the aggrieved copy can prove. Duplicate heads thus collapse to one identity at the zenith of verification. Each fake node must maintain a separate consistent history, costing full storage and compute per identity.
